Format EHT data to standard structure

format_eht_data.Rd

Transforms raw EHT data into standardized format required for analysis. Handles column renaming, derived variable calculation, and type coercion. Stops if a treatment code has more than one vector_control_product, since the extract functions would then duplicate rows when labelling results. The same product may appear under several codes (e.g. washed and unwashed).

Usage

format_eht_data(
  data,
  calculate_derived = TRUE,
  coerce_types = TRUE,
  control_value = NULL,
  mapping = NULL
)

Arguments

data

Data frame or tibble. Raw EHT data.

calculate_derived

Logical. If TRUE, calculate fed, dead, total columns.

coerce_types

Logical. If TRUE, coerce columns to appropriate types.

control_value

Value that identifies the control group in the treatment column. If NULL, attempts to detect automatically (looks for 0 or "control"). Numeric treatment columns are only re-encoded when control_value is given (e.g. control_value = 1 for data coded 1, 2, 3).

mapping

List. Custom column name mapping passed to standardize_column_names, e.g. list(UA = "alive", FA = "alivefed"). Each element is named with the standard column name and contains the source name(s) in the data.

Value

Formatted tibble with standardized structure:

  • Endpoints (UA, UD, FA, FD) as numeric

  • treatment as integer (0 = control, 1+ = treatments)

  • vector_control_product as character (if present; otherwise created from text treatment labels before they are encoded)

  • Derived variables: fed, dead, total (if calculate_derived = TRUE)

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
# Format raw data
data_formatted <- format_eht_data(raw_data)

# Specify control group
data_formatted <- format_eht_data(raw_data, control_value = "untreated")

# Map non-standard column names
data_formatted <- format_eht_data(raw_data,
  mapping = list(UA = "alive", UD = "dead", FA = "alivefed", FD = "deadfed"))
} # }
